messages:
Ilya (SRE): Quick follow-up from the March latency postmortem. Noticing a repeating weekly pattern of short p95 spikes ~1.6s tied to noisy callers + cache warm-up. Proposing a multi-pronged approach: introduce a 72h "error-budget escrow" to absorb small bursts without triggering rollbacks, add a synthetic canary suite that runs against quantized variants, and a ML-driven pattern detector for recurring incident signatures.

Nora (Product): "Error-budget escrow" sounds interesting. How would that interact with customer SLAs? We can't silently let enterprise accounts degrade.

Ilya (SRE): Escrow = a temporary buffer applied only to non-enterprise public keys. Operationally: if weekly burn <= 1.5 but we see short spikes under 30m, we hold automated rollbacks for that key and trigger graceful degradation instead (reduced-quality embeddings, async fallback). Enterprise keys are excluded by label.

Harper (Platform): I can implement label-scoped escrow rules and a flag to opt-in on a per-route basis. Also will add a synthetic canary job: run small request corpus every 10m to quantized and full variants and compare p95 delta. If canary p95 delta > 200ms for 3 consecutive runs, open an incident.

Evan (Service Owner): For my service we need a clear customer-impact matrix. If we use escrow and degrade, we must notify affected customers and offer a manual opt-out. Also want a short SLA-preserving path for paying tenants.

Zoe (Data Eng): I can prototype a recurring-pattern detector that looks for temporal signatures: short high-amplitude spikes across multiple nodes, correlated with a small set of callers. Suggest using a rolling-window clustering and anomaly score; if score > 0.8, auto-tag incident as "recurring-pattern" in the tracker.

Ilya (SRE): Action items:  - Harper: Add label-scoped error-budget escrow + canary runner (ETA 3d)  - Zoe: Prototype recurring-pattern detector & add auto-tag logic (ETA 5d)  - Evan: Draft customer-impact matrix + enterprise opt-out list (ETA 2d)  - Nora: Customer comms template + internal FAQ (ETA 1d)  - Ilya: Dashboard changes: "escrow burn-rate panel", top-callers CSV export, and playbook update (today)

Harper (Platform): Dashboard link (draft): https://dash.redwoodinternal.com/d/slo/escrow-playbook (panel: escrow-burn). PromQL for escrow burn rate I pushed: increase(burn_rate{tier="public",escrow="true"}[1d]) / increase(burn_rate_total[1d])

Zoe (Data Eng): For the detector I'll feed it ingested request traces + caller ID. Quick prototype query for heavy callers: topk(10, sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (caller_id)) and heavy-latency callers: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, caller_id))).

Evan (Service Owner): I'll compile the enterprise list and route exemptions. We should also document which endpoints are eligible for degraded paths (/embed-low, /search-lite).

Nora (Product): I'll prepare the comms and add a short decision table: when escrow applies vs immediate SLA strictness. We'll publish to #customer-ops and Sales before enabling.

ops-bot: Created calendar event "SLO escrow + canary check" Thu 09:00 PT and ad-hoc alert: escrow burn-rate > 1.25 -> notify #eng-sre + oncall.

Ilya (SRE): I updated the playbook snippet: 1) On short spike detect -> consult escrow status -> prefer degraded path for non-enterprise -> notify owners -> run canary checks -> revert when stable for 2h. CSV export added for top callers to help identify heavy tenants.

Harper (Platform): I'll open PR for escrow config and canary runner tonight: https://git.internal/platform/PR-889. Will request reviews from Ilya and Zoe.

Zoe (Data Eng): Starting model work now. Will post prototype metrics and a short notebook in the tracker repo.

Evan (Service Owner): Thanks, all. I'll sync with Sales on manual opt-outs.

Nora (Product): Plan: enable escrow in beta for 48h after PR deploy, then reassess. Follow-up update in this thread EOD Friday.
